description: Hello! We're looking for teammates. Our team consists of a Full-Stack developer, a math and space enthusiast, and a versatile Python data specialist. We have a solid technical foundation to build our product. To complete the group, we need UI/UX designers, communicators for pitching, and creative minds. If you want a collaborative environment where ideas quickly turn into real code, send us a message!
summary:
Mission Health Control is a browser-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed for autonomous crew care during deep-space missions. Inspired by NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) and Artemis-era exploration, it evaluates crew vital signs directly in the browser using deterministic clinical rules and three-tier escalation (self-care, crew attention, ground flight surgeon) without blocking on real-time ground servers.
The platform integrates live solar flare telemetry from NASA’s DONKI API (with CCMC and local fallbacks), an interactive anatomical body map with plain-language hazard guidance, multi-scale telemetry charts (from 60-day trends down to 5-second windows), stackable emergency simulations and behavioral/cognitive assessments including a reaction-time test, a 5×5 memory grid, and a NASA-inspired mental wellness survey.
As communication delays scale from 0.5 seconds in LEO to 22 minutes on Mars, astronauts must act as their own first responders—a model equally valuable for remote healthcare on Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Mission Health Control is a prototype medical telemetry and decision-support console for astronauts operating across five mission environments: Space Station (LEO), Deep-Space Transit Spacecraft, Surface Rover, Lunar South-Pole Base, and Mars Surface Base.

Rather than requiring medical expertise from the crew, the software executes a deterministic clinical rules engine (evaluateHealth()) directly in the browser:

  1. Environment-Aware Risk & Latency Context: Switching mission environments dynamically updates Earth communication latency (from ~0.5s in LEO to 8–22 minutes on Mars), dominant NASA spaceflight hazards, and clinical thresholds (such as stricter deep-space radiation limits and post-EVA lunar dust checks).
  2. Interactive Body System Map: Crew members click anatomical regions (Head/Neuro-behavioral, Heart/Cardiovascular, Abdomen/Metabolic, Limbs/Immune & Musculoskeletal) color-coded by a standard semaphore (Normal / Needs attention / Critical) to read plain-language explanations of why each hazard matters and what NASA HRP risks apply.
  3. Live Space Weather Integration (NASA DONKI): A backend route (/api/donki/flr) fetches real-time Solar Flare (FLR) telemetry from NASA DONKI (with CCMC mirror and mock ground-API fallbacks), surfaces mission flare alerts, and overlays GOES flare markers onto the radiation exposure timeline.
  4. Multi-Scale Telemetry & Historical Replay: Interactive charts track cardiovascular trends, recovery/metabolic drift, and daily/cumulative radiation exposure against NASA/CSA caution thresholds (1.0 mSv/day). Users can drill down from mission days to hourly, 1-minute, and 5-second windows using a layered synthetic telemetry archive (60 days of generated hot, minute-rollup, and hour-rollup data), plus click any historical point to replay the crew’s exact clinical state.
  5. Cognitive, Behavioral & Routine Countermeasures: Includes a 28-item NASA HRP-inspired mental wellness pool (sampling 8 questions per session), a 5×5 spatial memory grid, a millisecond cognitive reaction-time test, and a gamified daily countermeasure checklist (resistive exercise, hydration, sleep hygiene, dosimetry, cabin CO₂ checks) with persistence in localStorage.
  6. Stackable Emergency Simulations: A mission-simulation bar allows testing single or combined anomalies (Solar Particle Event, Cardio/Dehydration, Isolation & Circadian Drift) across a 10-astronaut simulated crew roster (/api/mission-feed).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Spaceflight Autonomy: Bridges the gap when real-time telemedicine with Earth flight surgeons is delayed or unavailable, empowering crews to triage symptoms early and follow clear escalation paths (Self-Care → Crew Attention → Ground Flight Surgeon).
  • Terrestrial Impact: The same low-bandwidth, client-side triage architecture is directly applicable to remote rural clinics, Antarctic/maritime expeditions, and isolated regions on Earth (such as rural communities in northern Argentina) with intermittent connectivity and limited on-site specialists.

Tools, Languages & Data Sources Used

  • Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript (strict mode), Tailwind CSS, daisyUI, Recharts, Lucide React, @emmorts/body-muscles, and @faker-js/faker (for deterministic synthetic crew telemetry).
  • Data & Scientific References: NASA DONKI Solar Flare API (and CCMC mirror), NASA Human Research Program (Spaceflight Hazards, Human Health Risks, Ongoing Research), and Canadian Space Agency (CSA radiation monitoring and ISS life sciences).
  • AI / Super Intelligence (SI) Transparency: AI coding assistants (Cursor Agent / LLMs) were used by the team to accelerate TypeScript scaffolding, synthetic telemetry generation, and slide/visual asset creation, with all clinical rules, architecture, and challenge design directed and verified by the team.

Creativity & Key Design Factors

  • Human-Centered Telemetry UI: Designed as a unified flight-surgeon console with bilingual support (English/Spanish), keyboard navigation, and live ARIA status announcements, ensuring clarity under high-stress conditions without assuming medical training.
  • Resilient Hybrid Architecture: Keeps all critical clinical evaluation deterministic in the browser while treating ground APIs (/api/health-log, /api/mental-health, /api/mission-feed, /api/donki/flr) as non-blocking enhancements with automatic fallbacks.

Future Work

  • Direct Bluetooth/BLE ingestion from flight wearables and personal dosimeters (e.g., Artemis ARCHeR-style biometrics and neutron spectrometers).
  • On-device computer-vision assistance for ocular ultrasound (SANS screening) and dermatological/immune rash checks.
  • Full Progressive Web App (PWA) service-worker caching and encrypted delay-tolerant sync bundles for intermittent deep-space links.
